sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 shows the southern corner of the Town of Union (Union Hill) between Hudson Avenue on the left and Bulls Ferry Road and Pleasant Avenue on the right, which form the boundary with Weehawken, from Franklin Street at the top down to the Hackensack Plank Road (turnpike), whose far side is also Weehawken. Weehawken and Cantelo Streets cross the sheet, and Kossuth Street runs diagonally parallel to the plank road. North points to the upper left. The upper blocks are dominated by the Wm. Peter Brewing Company: a large old brewery marked as not used, stock house and storage, a machine shop, cooper shop, oil room and brew house between Franklin and Weehawken Streets, and the company's bottling department across Weehawken Street. The Atlantic Garden, a saloon and beer garden with storage, fills the Bulls Ferry Road end of the same block. The middle of the sheet is thinly built, with many lots still vacant. The lower part is taken by the York Silk Company's Clifton Branch mill, a long group of winding, warping, spinning, doubling and finishing rooms set along Kossuth Street and the plank road, with a separate box noting its lighting, power and watch arrangements. Elsewhere there are dwellings, flats and a few stores, a garage and an automobile storage shed. Water pipes in Hudson Avenue and the plank road are drawn with their sizes. The boundary of the Town of Union and Weehawken is lettered along Pleasant Avenue and the plank road.
notes: Franklin is now 34th Street; Weehawken Street is now Peter Street; Cantelo is now Cantello Street; Kossuth is now the diagonal stretch of 33rd Street; Bulls Ferry Road is now Park Avenue; Hackensack Plank Road is now Plank Road here.
The area south of Cantelo was cut by the Lincoln Tunnel approach (Marginal Highways); few of the lower junctions survive.
Hudson Avenue jogs where it crosses the plank road; both crossings were used as control.

Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part. Hudson Av to Bulls Ferry Rd/Pleasant Av (Weehawken line), Franklin (34th) to Hackensack Plank Rd; Wm. Peter Brewing Co, York Silk Co. Lower area cut by Lincoln Tunnel approach.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers a strip of the Town of Union along its eastern boundary with Weehawken, between Hudson Avenue on the left and Bulls Ferry Road on the right, from Columbia Street at the top to Gardner Street at the bottom. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left of the page and the cross streets run across it. Six blocks are shown, divided by Main, Liberty, Humboldt and Morgan Streets. The Bulls Ferry Road side carries the town line, lettered Town of Union and Weehawken, and the blocks next to it are drawn only as far as the lot lines. The area is almost entirely residential: dwellings and flats on narrow lots, with frame and brick buildings mixed, and a few stores near the avenue. A garage and a row of attached brick houses stand near Bulls Ferry Road between Main and Liberty Streets. The Hackensack Water Company has premises on Morgan Street, and Grace Episcopal Church with its parish buildings stands in the block next to the town line below Morgan Street. Fire alarm boxes and hydrants are marked at corners. The Weehawken streets Columbia Terrace, Clifton Terrace and Highwood Avenue or Liberty Place are lettered at the edge. Part of the right side of the sheet is blank paper beyond the boundary.
notes: Cross streets renamed with numbers since: Columbia is 44th Street, Main is 43rd Street, Liberty is 42nd Street, Humboldt is 41st Street, Morgan is 40th Street, Gardner is 39th Street (Gardner and Morgan tied to sheet 43; the Weehawken names at Park Avenue match the east side of the town).
Bulls Ferry Road along the Weehawken line is Park Avenue today.
Sheet is turned: fitted rotation about -31 degrees.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 lies directly below sheet 33 and continues the same strip along the Weehawken line, between Hudson Avenue on the left and Bulls Ferry Road on the right, from Gardner Street at the top to Franklin Street at the bottom. Lewis, Union, Blum and Jefferson Streets cross between them. The page is turned so that north points to the upper right and the cross streets run across it. The strip holds mixed industry and housing. The Weehawken Granite Company, makers of laundry tubs, occupies a large block at the top beside Hudson Avenue, with a pearl button factory and lumber yards below Lewis Street. Near Bulls Ferry Road is the Gouled Embroidery Works, and a set of embroidery and textile buildings and a row of dwellings face the road. The remaining blocks are dwellings, flats and stores with a few vacant lots, most densely built along Hudson Avenue and Union Street. The town line is shown between Bulls Ferry Road and the Weehawken side, where Highwood Terrace is lettered. Beyond the line the paper is left blank. Water pipes and hydrants are marked at the corners.
notes: Cross streets renamed with numbers since: Gardner is 39th Street, Lewis is 38th Street, Union is 37th Street, Blum is 36th Street, Jefferson is 35th Street, Franklin is 34th Street (Gardner tied to sheet 33 and Franklin to sheet 32 by the Hudson Avenue spacing).
Bulls Ferry Road along the Weehawken line is Park Avenue today.
Sheet is turned: fitted rotation about -31 degrees.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 covers the south-western corner of the Town of Union (Union Hill), a wedge between the Hackensack Plank Road (turnpike), which here forms the boundary with West Hoboken, and Franklin Street on the right, from Bergenline Avenue at the top of the sheet to Hudson Avenue at the bottom, with New York Avenue and Palisade Avenue crossing it. Kossuth Street runs diagonally through the middle, parallel to the plank road, so the blocks along both are cut obliquely. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right. West Hoboken beyond the plank road is left blank apart from the lettered names of Spring Street and Clinton Avenue. The blocks are dense with dwellings, flats and stores with flats above, several bowling alleys and saloons; the Bergenline Avenue frontage is marked as drawn from plans. Institutions include the German Evangelical Lutheran Church on New York Avenue, the Pioneer Hose Company No. 1 fire house, and the Temple Emanuel Synagogue near Kossuth Street. Commerce and trades include the Reiling and Schoen warehouse and a livery stable on the plank road, a hay and feed store, and wagon sheds, an office and a horse hospital of the Wm. Peter Brewing Company between Palisade and Hudson Avenues. Cantelo Street and Weehawken Street are lettered below Hudson Avenue, where they continue onto sheet 32. Water pipes and their sizes are drawn in the streets.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is now the diagonal stretch of 32nd Street (the old West Hoboken boundary); Kossuth is now the diagonal stretch of 33rd Street; Franklin is now 34th Street; Weehawken Street is now Peter Street; Cantelo Street is now Cantello Street.
Bergenline Avenue frontage marked (From Plans).

Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part. Wedge between Hackensack Plank Rd (32nd St diagonal, West Hoboken line) and Franklin (34th), Bergenline to Hudson Av; Kossuth = 33rd St diagonal.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 covers four to five blocks of the centre of the Town of Union between Bergenline Avenue at the top and Hudson Avenue at the bottom, and between Franklin Street on the left and Union Street on the right, with New York Avenue and Palisade Avenue running across the middle. Jefferson and Blum Streets divide the blocks. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right and the avenues run across the page. Bergenline Avenue and New York Avenue carry the stores, with flats above, and the large blocks behind hold dwellings and flats. Institutions include Public School No. 3 near Hudson Avenue at the lower left, the Evangelical Lutheran St. Johannes Church near New York Avenue, the Modern Institute, and a hall in the block next to Union Street. Commercial and industrial premises are the New York and New Jersey Telephone Company exchange, the United Bottling Company (mineral waters) on Jefferson Street, the Jefferson Livery, a bowling alley and the lumber yard of J. W. Fink and Company near Hudson Avenue. The area north of Bergenline Avenue shows the ends of Franklin Lane and Jefferson, Blum and Union Places. Fire alarm boxes and water pipes are marked throughout.
notes: Cross streets renamed with numbers since: Franklin is 34th Street, Jefferson is 35th Street, Blum is 36th Street, Union is 37th Street (Union and Franklin tied to sheets 43 and 32).
Blum and Union Streets jog at Bergenline Avenue against Blum and Union Places to the north; modern 36th and 37th Streets cross Bergenline Avenue 12 m and 5 m from the drawn junctions.
Sheet is turned: fitted rotation about +59 degrees.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 is a wedge-shaped sheet along the north side of Bergenline Avenue at the western boundary of the Town of Union with West Hoboken. The Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) runs diagonally up the left side of the sheet as the town line, and Franklin Lane and Jefferson Place run up the sheet from Bergenline Avenue, narrowing the land between them as the plank road and the lanes converge toward Hudson Boulevard West at the top right. Most of the left side of the sheet, in West Hoboken, is blank. Bergenline Avenue at the bottom is lined with a continuous row of brick stores with flats above, among them a bank at the plank road corner, furniture and other shops, and a candy factory. Behind them the blocks between Franklin Lane and Jefferson Place hold dwellings, a textile embroidery works, the Gesellen Verein club house, an embroidery factory and the Holy Family Parochial School. Along the West Hoboken line the lots narrow into long strips with houses. Central Avenue and Summit Avenue are lettered on the West Hoboken side. Franklin Street, Kossuth Street and Jefferson Street are shown across Bergenline Avenue at the bottom edge. The sheet is rotated so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road here is the diagonal stretch of 32nd Street today; Jefferson Place is 35th Street; Franklin Lane is not a modern street, but 34th Street meets Bergenline Avenue at its foot (tie: the spacing from the plank road junction matches sheet 36's Franklin Street).
Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard today.
Few junctions survive in the modern network; the fit rests on six points with a leave-one-out error of about 5 m.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 shows the blocks west of Bergenline Avenue in the Town of Union, from Bergenline Avenue at the bottom to Hudson Boulevard West near the top, between Jefferson Place on the left and Lewis Street on the right, with Blum Place and Union Place between them. The sheet is rotated so that north points to the upper right. Four long blocks run back from Bergenline Avenue, built with dwellings and flats on narrow lots and a continuous row of brick stores along the avenue frontage, among them the R. Holthusen department store. The Holy Family Church stands in the left-hand block, and the American Dry Ornamental Company and the lamp works of Wm. Stevenhagen are on Jefferson Place. The Union Place Methodist Episcopal Church and a bowling alley and hall are in the blocks further right. A number of lots near the boulevard are vacant. Above Hudson Boulevard West the sheet is blank, and the diagonal West Hoboken line and the plank road cross the top left corner. Blum Street and Union Street are lettered across Bergenline Avenue at the bottom.
notes: Names renamed with numbers since: Jefferson Place is 35th Street, Blum Place is 36th Street, Union Place is 37th Street, Lewis is 38th Street (tied to sheet 39 and sheet 43).
Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard today.
Blum and Union Places jog against Blum and Union Streets across Bergenline Avenue; 36th Street at Bergenline Avenue and the 37th Street junction were left out of the fit.
Four control points only; scale fits 0.9 percent below the other sheets.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 covers a thinly built wedge of the Town of Union (Union Hill) west of Hudson Boulevard West, between the boulevard at the bottom of the sheet and the Hackensack Plank Road (turnpike) at the top, which here is the boundary with North Bergen. The two roads converge at the left edge. Jefferson Place, Blum Place, Union Place and Lewis Street run from the boulevard up to the plank road. North points to the upper right. Most of the sheet is open lots with scattered frame dwellings, many of them small and set back from the street; the blocks between Union Place and Lewis Street are the most fully built, with rows of dwellings, flats and a saloon. The largest building is the Schwarzenbach, Huber and Company silk mill on the corner of Blum Place and the boulevard, a weaving mill with its office, engine house, chimney and a rooftop water tank, described in a separate box below the boulevard (lighting, power, heating, watchman and pumps). The J. P. Nawrath and Company mop factory stands on Blum Place. Near the junction of the two roads at the left edge there is a curved group of buildings and a small greenhouse or shed. Beyond the plank road the North Bergen side is blank. Water pipes in the boulevard and the plank road are drawn with their sizes.
notes: Hudson Boulevard West is now John F. Kennedy Boulevard; the Hackensack Plank Road here is now Bergen Turnpike.
Blum Place, Union Place and Lewis Street are now 36th, 37th and 38th Streets west of the boulevard.
Placed from four detected junctions at 37th and 38th Streets only (ink threshold 100); the left (south-western) end of the sheet is extrapolated.

Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part. West of Hudson Blvd West up to Hackensack Plank Rd (Bergen Turnpike, North Bergen line); sparse; Schwarzenbach Huber silk mill. Weak: 4 points, ink 100.

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 lies at the north-western corner of the Town of Union, on the boundary with North Bergen. The Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) crosses the upper part of the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right, and the Town of Union and North Bergen boundary line runs along it and then down the right side of the sheet. Lewis Street and Gardner Street run south from the plank road to Hudson Boulevard West, which crosses the lower part of the sheet; Morgan Street is lettered below the boulevard at the right. The sheet is rotated so that north points to the upper right. Most of the area is open lots laid out in long narrow strips, with scattered dwellings along Lewis Street and near the plank road and a few buildings along Gardner Street. The largest works is the Peerless Granite Company, makers of laundry tubs, in a block between Gardner and Morgan Streets by Hudson Boulevard West, with a wagon shed and some small buildings near it. Palisade Cemetery is lettered at the right edge, and Secaucus Road is lettered at a side road near the plank road at the top.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road here is Bergen Turnpike today; Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard; Lewis is 38th Street and Gardner is 39th Street.
Four control points; the Morgan Street junction with the boulevard was not detected. Low confidence.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 shows the area west of Bergenline Avenue between Bergenline Avenue at the bottom and Hudson Boulevard West at the top, from Lewis Street on the left to Humboldt Street at the right edge, with Gardner and Morgan Streets between. The sheet is rotated so that north points to the upper right, and the town line with North Bergen crosses the top right corner. The centre of the sheet is taken by the large silk mill of R. and H. Simon, drawn in pink as brick fire-resistive buildings fitted with automatic sprinklers, and marked as a Mutual Risk diagram from plans, with a boiler house, engine room and storage buildings; the firm's garage and chemical and storage buildings stand to the left. Other buildings are the West Shore Laundry and a plumber's shop. The remaining blocks hold flats and dwellings on narrow lots, with a continuous row of brick stores along Bergenline Avenue. The upper left part, toward Hudson Boulevard West, is open lots with a few dwellings. A table of the sprinkler and fire protection of the Simon mill is printed above the boulevard.
notes: Streets renamed with numbers since: Lewis is 38th Street, Gardner is 39th Street, Morgan is 40th Street, Humboldt is 41st Street (tied to sheet 43 and sheet 33).
Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard today.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 covers the western edge of the Town of Union (Union Hill) between Hudson Boulevard West, which forms the boundary with North Bergen on the left of the sheet, and Bergenline Avenue on the right, from Fulton Street at the top down to Humboldt Street at the bottom. Van Vorst, John, Main and Liberty Streets cross the sheet between them, and Harrison Place and Cottage Place are lettered running north from Fulton Street. North points to the upper left. The five blocks are long and narrow and almost entirely residential: rows of frame dwellings, flats and a few saloons and stores, with stores and flats concentrated on the Bergenline Avenue frontage, including a bakery. A row of attached dwellings with bay fronts lines the north side of Van Vorst Street. The main industrial building is the Julius Schwarz embroidery works on Humboldt Street near Bergenline Avenue, with its lighting, heating and power noted. A hose company fire house stands on John Street near Bergenline Avenue. Many lots remain vacant, particularly in the upper blocks toward Fulton Street. The North Bergen and Town of Union boundary is lettered along Hudson Boulevard West, and Mark Lane is lettered beyond the boulevard at the top left. Water pipes are drawn in the cross streets.
notes: West of Bergenline Avenue the cross streets are now: Fulton = 45th Street, Van Vorst = 44th Street, John = Lincoln Street, Main = 43rd Street, Liberty = 42nd Street, Humboldt = 41st Street.
Hudson Boulevard West is now John F. Kennedy Boulevard.

Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part. Hudson Blvd West (Kennedy Blvd) to Bergenline, Fulton (45th) to Humboldt (41st); streets jog at Bergenline (John = Lincoln St).

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 covers four blocks in the centre of the Town of Union (Union Hill), between Bergenline Avenue at the top of the sheet and Hudson Avenue at the bottom, and between Union Street on the left and Morgan Street on the right, with New York Avenue and Palisade Avenue running across the middle. Lewis and Gardner Streets divide the blocks. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right; the avenues run across the page. This was the civic and commercial heart of the town. The Town Hall, which also housed the high school on its upper floors, stands on Palisade Avenue between Union and Lewis Streets, beside the Olympic Athletic Club. Nearby on New York Avenue are Turner Hall with its gymnasium and the Hudson Theater, an auditorium seating about 1300, with the Hendrik Hudson Hotel behind it on Lewis Street. Public School No. 1 fills much of the block between Bergenline and New York Avenues east of Gardner Street, and St. Augustine's Roman Catholic church, rectory and parochial school occupy the next block toward Palisade Avenue, together with the North Hudson Hospital and the First Baptist Church. Industry is small: the New Idea Manufacturing Company (novelties and silver plating), a knitting works and moving-picture rooms behind the Bergenline Avenue frontage, the Gardner and Meeks lumber yard near Hudson Avenue and the Thomas Henry building materials yard between Palisade and Hudson Avenues. The rest is dwellings, flats and stores with flats above, densest along Bergenline Avenue. Water pipes and fire alarm boxes are marked at the corners.
notes: Cross streets renamed with numbers since: Union is 37th Street, Lewis is 38th Street, Gardner is 39th Street, Morgan is 40th Street (confirmed by the Town Hall site, now Union City Hall at 3715 Palisade Avenue, and by the Weehawken street names on sheet 33).
The town hall here also held the high school on its second and third floors.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part. Pilot. Bergenline to Hudson Av, Union (37th) to Morgan (40th); Town Hall, Public School No. 1.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 covers the middle of the Town of Union (Union Hill) between Bergenline Avenue at the top and Hudson Avenue at the bottom, and from Morgan Street on the left to Main Street on the right, with Humboldt and Liberty Streets between them. New York Avenue and Palisade Avenue run across the sheet, so it shows three rows of blocks. North points to the upper right and the avenues run across the page. The blocks are mostly dwellings and flats, packed along the avenue frontages and looser toward the middle of each block, with stores and saloons at the corners and a scattering of vacant lots. The larger buildings are few. E. Riethmann's embroidery works stands on the block between Bergenline and New York Avenues, near Humboldt Street, and a bottling works is on the next block east. Michel and Rank, printers, occupy the lower end of the block west of Humboldt Street on New York Avenue. F. Pirl's wagon works, a livery stable with a long frame stable range, a cooper shop and a print shop are among the trade buildings between New York and Hudson Avenues, and a bakery fronts the Palisade Avenue side. Pink-coloured rows of stores and flats stand on Palisade Avenue near Liberty Street. The blocks south of Hudson Avenue are left blank and carry the number of sheet 33. Water pipes are drawn in the streets with their sizes, and hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked at several corners.
notes: Cross streets are now numbered: Morgan is 40th Street, Humboldt is 41st Street, Liberty is 42nd Street, Main is 43rd Street (Morgan tied to sheet 43, which borders this sheet on the left).
Avenue names are unchanged.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 covers the part of the Town of Union (Union Hill) east of Main Street as far as Fulton Street, between Bergenline Avenue at the top and Hudson Avenue at the bottom, with Columbia Street between Main and Fulton. New York Avenue and Palisade Avenue cross the sheet. North points to the upper right and the avenues run across the page. John Street and Van Vorst Place are lettered on the blocks north of Bergenline Avenue at the top of the sheet. The two upper rows of blocks hold a mix of institutions and dwellings: the Public Library at Main Street and New York Avenue, the German Evangelical Church with its heating and lighting noted, and the Masonic Temple at the right end of the Bergenline Avenue frontage, whose lower floors are stores. Bergenline Avenue has a nearly continuous row of stores with flats above. Along Palisade Avenue and between it and Hudson Avenue stand the Littauer Oil Company (salad and cooking oils), a hook and ladder company house marked Dispatch, bowling alleys, a wagon painter and wagon storage, a tile, slate and marble works and a stone yard, with ordinary dwellings and flats on the remaining lots. Most blocks are fully built along the street fronts, with open ground in the middle. The sheet overlaps sheet 43 on the left (sheet 44 is the number printed there) and sheet 46 on the right. Fire alarm boxes, hydrants and water pipe sizes are marked in the streets.
notes: Cross streets are now numbered: Main is 43rd Street, Columbia is 44th Street, Fulton is 45th Street (Columbia and Fulton also appear on sheet 48 at the Weehawken line).
John Street and Van Vorst Place are lettered only where they meet Bergenline Avenue from the west; sheet 42 shows them as Lincoln Street and 44th Street today.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 covers the east side of the Town of Union (Union Hill) between Bergenline Avenue at the top and Hudson Avenue at the bottom, from the block east of Fulton Street on the left to 3rd Street at the right. Golden Lane and Cleveland Place run down from Bergenline Avenue, and 1st, 2nd and 3rd Streets cross the lower half of the sheet. North points to the upper right and the avenues run across the page. New York Avenue and Palisade Avenue are not drawn through this sheet; the ground between Bergenline and Hudson Avenues is divided into a few long blocks. The upper blocks are sparsely built. Bergenline Avenue has a row of stores and flats, and at its centre a moving picture theatre with an open air theatre and stage behind it. Near the middle of the sheet stand a greenhouse range and the large Consumers Hygienic Ice Company plant, with its ice storage, freezing and ammonia works, boiler house and a siding, beside a milk depot and a plumber. Rows of flats and two and three storey dwellings, many of them pink or yellow, line 2nd and 3rd Streets, and bowling alleys and a block of attached flats face the right edge. The blocks near Hudson Avenue are built with ordinary dwellings and flats and some vacant lots. The sheet number 48 is printed below Hudson Avenue. A scale of feet is printed at the bottom right, and a section of 3rd Street is lettered Third Street where it crosses Bergenline Avenue at the top right.
notes: 2nd Street is now 46th Street and 3rd Street is now 47th Street, tied to the old 3rd Street on sheets 47, 48 and 50 and to the Fulton and Columbia Street spacing on sheet 48; 1st Street has no modern counterpart (the old Fulton Street, now 45th Street, lies one block west, about 480 ft from 46th Street along Hudson Avenue).
Golden Lane and Cleveland Place no longer exist as named streets; neither is in the OpenStreetMap extract.
New York Avenue and Palisade Avenue pass through this area today but are not drawn as streets on the sheet; the part is placed on Hudson Avenue and Bergenline Avenue junctions only.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 covers the north-western corner of the Town of Union (Union Hill) west of Bergenline Avenue. Hudson Boulevard West, the boundary with North Bergen, runs down the left side and Bergenline Avenue down the right; Fulton Street is at the bottom of the sheet and 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets cross it going up, with Harrison Place and Cottage Place running north from Fulton Street between them. North points to the upper left and the sheet is turned so that the avenues run up the page. At the top the sheet reaches the West New York boundary line, beyond which the margin refers to Volume 8A. The Bergenline Avenue frontage is the busiest part: stores with flats above, a bank (the Weehawken Trust Company) and insurance offices at 5th Street, and the Engine Company No. 2 volunteer fire house with its hose house and alarm at 4th Street. Wagon sheds, a sheet metal works and a laundry are drawn near Bergenline Avenue. The blocks along Hudson Boulevard West are lined with frame dwellings and a few flats, set on narrow lots with some vacant ground, and the middle blocks between 4th and 3rd Streets hold scattered dwellings and outbuildings. A large part of the block between 5th and 4th Streets is drawn as ruled lot lines with only a few buildings. Water pipes, fire alarm boxes and hydrants are marked in the streets, and a scale of feet is printed at the bottom left.
notes: Fulton is now 45th Street, 3rd Street is now 47th Street, 4th Street is now 48th Street and 5th Street is now 49th Street (west of Bergenline Avenue, tied to sheet 42 for Fulton and to sheet 50 for 3rd to 5th Streets).
Hudson Boulevard West is now John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 covers the north-eastern end of the Town of Union (Union Hill) between Hudson Avenue on the left and Bulls Ferry Road on the right, which is the boundary with Weehawken. Brown Street and Broadway run down the sheet and 3rd Street crosses the top; Fulton and Columbia Streets cross near the bottom. North points to the upper right and the sheet is turned so that the avenues run up the page. The rows of two and three storey flats and dwellings on Hudson Avenue and on Brown Street are drawn as continuous strips of narrow lots, with a long row of pink coloured attached houses on the east side of Brown Street. Broadway has flats, a milk depot with stable and a veterinary hospital. The largest works is the Daniel Bermes Brewery between Fulton and Columbia Streets, with its lettered buildings (brew house, boiler house, cold storage, malt, cooper shop, machine shop, ice machine) and its watchman's clock and pump, together with a reservoir; the legend printed below Columbia Street describes its fire protection. Hofman Brothers, a steam heated and lighted works, stands on Fulton Street. Bulls Ferry Road runs diagonally across the right side with the Town of Union and Weehawken boundary line lettered along it; beyond it the Weehawken blocks of Columbia Terrace and 1st Street are drawn, with the sheet numbers 65, 67 and 33 printed in the margins.
notes: Fulton is now 45th Street, Columbia is now 44th Street and 3rd Street is now 47th Street; Bulls Ferry Road is now Park Avenue; Brown is now Brown Street.
Park Avenue has two stretches side by side in OpenStreetMap near the Weehawken line; the junctions with 47th, 45th and 44th Streets fit within about 1.5 m.
1st Street and Columbia Terrace are Weehawken streets lettered beyond the boundary line.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 covers the north-eastern end of the Town of Union (Union Hill) between Bergenline Avenue at the top and Hudson Avenue at the bottom, from 3rd Street on the left to 5th Street at the right, with Palisade Avenue crossing the middle. North points to the upper right and the avenues run across the page. The right margin is the West New York boundary line, lettered along the edge, with a See Volume 8A note at the top. 4th and 5th Streets are lettered on the blocks north of Bergenline Avenue and the upper part of the sheet holds Public School No. 2, a large block with its yard and the school building heated by furnace and lit by gas. On Bergenline Avenue stand stores with flats above and the Weehawken Trust Company, and in the middle of the block between 4th and 5th Streets a small octagonal building is marked as a West Shore Railroad tunnel shaft. The blocks between Palisade and Hudson Avenues are dense rows of two and three storey dwellings and flats, with a few stores on the avenue frontages. Several blocks above Palisade Avenue near 3rd Street are filled with rows of identical houses, and open lots remain in the centre of the blocks. Water pipes are drawn in the streets with their sizes and fire alarm boxes are marked at corners. A scale of feet is printed at the bottom left and the sheet number 50 is printed below Hudson Avenue.
notes: 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets are now 47th, 48th and 49th Streets (tied to sheet 50, which draws the same streets at the Weehawken line).
The Bergenline Avenue junctions fit about 3 m from the rest because the modern parcel centre there lies 11 m from the OpenStreetMap node.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part.

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 covers the north-eastern corner of the Town of Union (Union Hill) between Hudson Avenue at the top of the sheet and Bulls Ferry Road at the bottom, which here is the boundary with Weehawken, and from 3rd Street on the left to just beyond 5th Street on the right, where the boundary with West New York is lettered; the area beyond is left blank with a See Volume note. Broadway crosses the middle of the sheet and Brown Street runs off 3rd Street at the left edge. North points to the upper right. The blocks are mainly residential: dwellings, flats and stores with flats above, with a few saloons, insurance offices and a drug store, and a row of buildings on Broadway at 4th Street marked as being built. A magazine printing works stands on 3rd Street near Bulls Ferry Road, and there is a hall on Bulls Ferry Road near 3rd Street. Many lots are still vacant, particularly between Hudson Avenue and Broadway and along the Bulls Ferry Road frontage. The Town of Union and Weehawken boundary line is lettered along Bulls Ferry Road, and water pipes are drawn with their sizes in the streets.
notes: 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets are now 47th, 48th and 49th Streets; Bulls Ferry Road is now Park Avenue.
A See Volume note in the right margin refers the area beyond the West New York line to another volume.
Town of Union (Union Hill, now northern Union City), Hudson County vol. 8A; 50 ft to an inch; one part. Hudson Av to Bulls Ferry Rd (Park Av), 3rd-5th Sts (= 47th-49th) to West New York line.
